subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which statement about light microscopes compared with electron microscopes is correct?
options: Light microscopes are cheaper and can view living specimens
Light microscopes have higher magnification and resolution
Light microscopes can show the inside detail of organelles clearly
Light microscopes use beams of electrons to form an image
questions.explain: Light microscopes are cheaper and can be used to look at living cells, but have lower magnification and resolution than electron microscopes.

questions.q: As you move a lamp further from pondweed, the rate of photosynthesis...
questions.explain: Moving the lamp away lowers light intensity, so the rate of photosynthesis decreases.

questions.q: Which substance is broken down in respiration to release energy?
questions.explain: Glucose is broken down in respiration to transfer energy for the cell.

questions.q: How are leaves adapted for efficient photosynthesis?
options: Broad and thin with stomata and many chloroplasts
Thick and narrow with no stomata
questions.explain: Leaves are broad and thin with a large surface area, stomata for gas exchange and many chloroplasts.

questions.q: A cell appears 40 mm wide under a microscope at a magnification of ×400. What is its actual width?
questions.explain: Actual size = image size ÷ magnification = 40 ÷ 400 = 0.1 mm.

questions.q: Why must a Biuret test for protein be carried out without heating, unlike the Benedict's test?
options: Because protein is destroyed by Benedict's solution
Because protein only forms in the cold
Because heating turns all proteins into sugars
Because the Biuret test gives its colour change at room temperature
questions.explain: The Biuret test produces a purple/lilac colour at room temperature, so heating is not required (unlike Benedict's test for sugars).

questions.q: Which of these is the smallest and would need the highest magnification to be seen?
questions.explain: A mitochondrion is a sub-cellular organelle and is smaller than a whole bacterium or animal cell.

questions.q: Which gas is needed for aerobic respiration?
questions.explain: Aerobic respiration requires oxygen to break down glucose fully.

questions.q: Light intensity, carbon dioxide concentration and temperature are known as...
questions.explain: These three are the main limiting factors that can control the rate of photosynthesis.

questions.q: Anaerobic respiration means respiration that takes place...
questions.explain: Anaerobic respiration is the release of energy from glucose without using oxygen.

questions.q: The optimum temperature for most human enzymes is about:
questions.explain: Most human enzymes work best at around body temperature, 37°C.

questions.q: Why does anaerobic respiration release less energy than aerobic respiration per glucose molecule?
options: Glucose is only partially broken down
questions.explain: Without oxygen glucose is incompletely broken down, so less energy is released.

questions.q: A cell is 0.05 mm wide. What is this in micrometres (µm)?
Starch is a large carbohydrate. What smaller molecules is it made from?
questions.explain: Carbohydrates such as starch are made up of simple sugar units like glucose.

questions.q: Which equation represents anaerobic respiration in yeast?
questions.explain: In yeast, glucose is converted to ethanol and carbon dioxide during fermentation.

questions.q: Enzymes are best described as:
options: Biological catalysts that speed up reactions
questions.explain: Enzymes are biological catalysts; they speed up reactions and are not used up.

questions.q: Aerobic respiration releases more energy per glucose molecule than anaerobic respiration because...
options: glucose is completely broken down using oxygen
questions.explain: With oxygen, glucose is fully broken down, releasing much more energy than anaerobic respiration.

questions.q: What is produced by anaerobic respiration in human muscles?
questions.explain: Anaerobic respiration in muscle cells produces lactic acid.

questions.q: Why do palisade cells near the top of a leaf contain many chloroplasts?
options: To absorb maximum light for photosynthesis
questions.explain: Palisade mesophyll cells are packed with chloroplasts to capture as much light as possible.

questions.q: What is the main reason living cells need to respire?
options: To release energy for life processes
questions.explain: Respiration releases energy needed for processes such as movement, growth and keeping warm.

questions.q: In which organelle does most aerobic respiration occur?
questions.explain: Aerobic respiration takes place mainly in the mitochondria.

questions.q: How could you show that small organisms such as germinating seeds are respiring?
options: They release carbon dioxide and warmth
questions.explain: Respiring seeds release carbon dioxide and energy as heat, which can be detected experimentally.

specSource: OCR GCSE (9–1) Biology (Gateway A) (J247) specification; Cell Level Systems
